analysis.investment_thesis: Aequs is a capital-hungry, loss-making contract manufacturer trading at fantasy valuations (288x EV/EBITDA) with no visible path to profitability — this is speculation, not investment. Despite the aerospace tailwind from India's defence push, the fundamentals are too broken to justify entry at any price near current levels.
key_strengths: Aerospace/defence sector structural tailwind via Make in India and PLI schemes
Promoter holding at 59% — skin in the game with founder-led heritage since 2000
Gross margin of 56% suggests the underlying manufacturing model has pricing power if costs are controlled
key_risks: Persistent losses (net loss of -110, -14, -102 Cr across 3 years) with 2025 deterioration despite improved scale
Free cash flow deeply negative and worsening (-76, -175, -239 Cr); CWIP jumped to 395 Cr with no clear return on invested capital
Dangerously high valuation (1,140x forward P/E, 288x EV/EBITDA) for a loss-making industrial — any disappointment means catastrophic drawdown
red_flags: Revenue actually declined in FY25 (965→925 Cr) while EBITDA collapsed 65% from 163→57 Cr — execution is deteriorating, not improving
D/E of 1.08 with 64-69 Cr annual finance costs eating into already thin operating income; negative reserves until FY25
Conglomerate business mix (aerospace + toys + cookware + warehousing + real estate clusters) suggests lack of focus — classic value destroyer in Indian markets
Negative ROE (-11.2%) and near-zero ROCE (1.1%) at market cap of 11,202 Cr is wealth destruction dressed up as a growth story
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aequs has an interesting macro story — India's aerospace & defence manufacturing ecosystem is real, and industrial cluster models can compound well. But the financials tell a painful truth: three consecutive years of net losses, operating margins in negative territory (-1.84%), and free cash flow burning ₹239 Cr in FY25 alone. The CWIP surge to ₹395 Cr signals aggressive capacity addition, but with ROCE at 1.11%, existing capital is generating virtually no return. Revenue growth has stalled and reversed (FY24→FY25 down 4%), while EBITDA collapsed from ₹163 Cr to ₹57 Cr — this is not the trajectory of a business building toward profitability.

The valuation is the final dealbreaker. At ₹11,202 Cr market cap on ₹925 Cr revenue (P/S of 10x) and ₹57 Cr EBITDA (EV/EBITDA of 288x), the market has priced in flawless execution for the next decade. I have seen great Indian businesses at 40-50x EBITDA that eventually disappointed investors — 288x on a loss-making, multi-sector contract manufacturer is pure speculation. Mera niyam hai: jab tak business profitable nahi, tab tak koi baat nahi. When the promoter can show me two consecutive years of PAT profits, improving ROCE toward 12-15%, and FCF turning positive, I will revisit. Today, this is a AVOID.
